edit.description: The shared test home already owns the guard's invocation half (`run_guard`, :375) and, since 09a0a5ee, its payload half (`guard_write_payload` and siblings, :395-:425). It does not own the third half every guard case needs: the fixture lock. Add that writer beside them — one home rendering `<root>/.temper/lock.toml` from typed rows the crate already exports publicly (`drift::AssemblyFactRow`, `ClauseRow`, `KindFactRow`, and `RegistrationRow`, the one import to add) plus the four-column provenance row (`name`/`source_path`/`source_hash`/`emit_hash`) `emit`'s own `rollup_tables` (`src/drift.rs:547`) writes and no public type carries, so a fixture's deliberately unmatchable hashes stay expressible. The mode is spelled once here, as the assembly fact's `fact`/`value` columns. `write_lock` (:672) stays exactly as it is and is not the home for this: it runs `drift::emit`, which writes real projections at real hashes — the opposite of a guard fixture, whose whole point is a declared row whose file is absent or drifted.

Sixteen hand-spelled lock fixtures, each opening with the same `[[declaration.assembly]]\nfact = \"mode\"\nvalue = \"<mode>\"` literal: :1533, :1588, :1635, :1821, :1845, :1879, :1924, :2001, :2072, :2104, :2136, :2165, :2247, :2277, :2419, :2445. Five of them are already this suite's own partial homes for the job — `represented_rule_harness` (:1628), `manifest_guard_harness` (:1995), `settings_manifest_harness` (:2159), `container_owned_settings_harness` (:2239) and `settings_manifest_lock` (:2443) — and become callers of the shared writer rather than five spellings of one TOML vocabulary. Each site keeps its own declared rows: the `.rules/safety.md` out-of-`.claude` locus, the `mcp-server` + `hook` two-registration case, the `settings` container row with its kind row, the `root.reachable` clause row, and the mode-only lock at :2072.

Six more of the same literal: :522, :549, :595, :615, :894, :952. Three write a byte-identical `[[rule]]` row for `rust`/`.claude/rules/rust.md`, two more the same for `safety`. `post_edge_harness` (:883) is this suite's partial home and becomes a caller. The :952 case declares `value = \"clobber\"` on purpose — the closed-vocabulary refusal `mode_from_declarations` raises — so the shared writer takes the mode as a string, never a typed enum, or that case stops being expressible.

summary: The guard suites hand-spell the lock's own TOML at 22 sites, and a renamed mode column would leave every warn arm green over a lock that declares nothing.

tests.asserts: every guard fixture declares its enforcement mode and its rows through the shared writer; the block/warn/note arms and the container, registration and clause cases keep their current verdicts
the guard and post-edge fixtures build their locks through the same writer, the `clobber` case still reaching the vocabulary refusal

acceptance: `cargo test` green, and the fold is proven non-vacuous by mutation: renaming the assembly family's `fact`/`value` columns, or the `mode` fact's own name, in `src/` turns the guard suites red — today the warn and note arms stay green, since `mode_from_declarations` reads an absent fact as `EnforcementMode::default()`.
notes: Swept over the 1f6478a2..28f74ca7 window, which folded these same two suites' payloads (09a0a5ee) and writers' constants (015670f7). `EnforcementMode` defaults to Warn (`compose.rs:72`) and an absent `mode` fact takes that default (`:1463`), so the silent-degradation half is real, not hypothetical. The wider hand-spelled-lock class in acceptance.rs, emit.rs, lock_declaration_rows.rs and session_start.rs is deliberately out of scope. scoped at 28f74ca7
